To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal control policy for hybrid production-inventory systems with remanufacturing can be described by three state-dependent base-stock levels and that the optimal return acceptance level decreases with the remanufacturable inventory.

the optimal control policy for hybrid manufacturing/remanufactured production-inventory systems is characterized by a base-stock level for the manufacturing and remanufacturer and a state-dependent acceptance threshold.

(1) the optimal control policy for hybrid manufacturing/remanufactoring systems with returns is characterized by three state-dependent base-stock levels for manufacturing, remantufacturing and returns and (2) the optimal policy can be approximated well by several simple heuristic control rules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the coordination of the three main activities in a hybrid manufacturing/remanufactured system, namely production, remanufacture and returns acceptance.
the development of a queuing control model for hybrid manufacturing/remanufactured production-inventory systems and the design of heuristic control rules that perform well in practice.
the coordination of the three control variables: manufacturing, remanufacturer and returns acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, depending on the cost parameters, a hybrid system can be operated either by the optimal or one of the heuristic policies.
the heuristic policies perform very well in comparison to the optimal control policy.

the optimal policy performs best, followed by the policy based on the heuristic control rule for the returns acceptance threshold, the heuristic control rule based on the manufacturing and remanufacturer threshold and the heuristic control rule with a single threshold.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a framework to model and analyze the joint coordination of manufacturing and remanufacturer control in a hybrid system with returns and that we have developed several heuristics that perform well compared to the optimal policy.
we have shown that it is possible to coordinate manufacturing and remanufacturer with a return acceptance policy.
the optimal policy for the considered hybrid production-inventory problem is characterized by three state-dependent thresholds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in hybrid production-inventory systems, the optimal policy is not necessarily to always accept a returned product, but to sometimes reject it.
it pays to accept a return only when the remanufacturable inventory is empty.
the optimal control policy is very sensitive to the cost parameters, especially when the acceptance cost is high and the remanufacturing cost is low.
